'''Ricard Rubio Vives''' (born 21 October 1990) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Joventut Badalona]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. He became the youngest player ever to play in the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] on 15 October 2005, at age 14.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Ricky Rubio establece un nuevo récord al debutar en la ACB con catorce años|url=http://www.libertaddigital.com/php3/noticia.php3?cpn=1276263122|work=Libertad Digital|date=15 October 2005|access-date=14 August 2006|language=es|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312042248/http://www.libertaddigital.com/php3/noticia.php3?cpn=1276263122|archive-date=12 March 2007}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite magazine|first=Marty|last=Burns|title=NBA types will have their eyes on Spanish phenom Rubio at Olympics|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/marty_burns/08/07/rubio.olympics/|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=8 August 2008|access-date=8 August 2008|archive-date=26 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026114826/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/marty_burns/08/07/rubio.olympics/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Rubio made his [[EuroLeague]] debut on 24 October 2006, a few days after turning 16,<ref>{{cite web|title=Report - Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame/report?pcode=LFW&gamecode=7&seasoncode=E2006|website=Euroleague.net|date=21 May 2023|access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> making him [[List of youngest EuroLeague players since the 2000–01 season|one of the youngest players to play in the EuroLeague]].

On 25 June 2009, Rubio was drafted with the fifth pick in the first round of the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],<ref>NBA.com, [http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Timberwolves_Select_Ricky_Rubio_at_No5-090625.html Wolves Select Ricky Rubio at No. 5], accessed 20 July 2009.</ref> making him the first player born in the 1990s to be drafted by an NBA team. The Timberwolves had an agreement in principle with his Spanish team, [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]], to buy out his contract, but Rubio backed out of the deal.<ref name="Backing out">{{cite news|title=Kahn: Rubio not ready to jump to NBA|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4437300|website=ESPN.com|date=1 September 2009|access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> On 31 August 2009, Joventut traded the rights to Rubio to [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]],<ref name="Rubio to Barça">{{cite news|first1=Ric|last1=Bucher|first2=Chris|last2=Sheridan|title=Sources: Wolves can't work buyout|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4435861|name-list-style=amp|work=ESPN|date=31 August 2009|access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> and Rubio signed a six-year contract with FC Barcelona the following day.<ref name="Barça signing">{{cite web|title=REGAL FCB scores teen sensation Rubio|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2009-10-signings/i/55545/3694/regal-fcb-scores-teen-sensation-ricky-rubio|publisher=[[Euroleague]]|date=1 September 2009|access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> In 2011, Rubio joined the Timberwolves,<ref name="wojnarowski1">{{cite news|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|title=Sources: Rubio, T'wolves reach deal|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=aw-wojnarowski_ricky_rubio_deal_timberwolves_060111 |work=Yahoo! Sports|date=1 June 2011|access-date=1 June 2011}}</ref> and spent six seasons in Minnesota before being traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in June 2017. He signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in July 2019, before returning to Minnesota in 2020. Rubio was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in August 2021, but was dealt to the [[Indiana Pacers]] a month after suffering a season ending ACL injury in December.

In August 2023, Rubio announced he was taking a break from the sport to prioritise his mental health. In January 2024, he announced that he would be retiring from the NBA.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Krawczynski |first=Jon |date=2024-02-06 |title=Ricky Rubio reflects on his NBA career and the dark days that occurred: ‘I was lost’ |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5205201/2024/01/29/ricky-rubio-timberwolves-cavaliers-nba-retirement/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Joventut (2005–2009)===
[[File:Camiseta autografata de Ricky Rubio (2009).jpg|thumb|250px|Signed Ricky Rubio jersey (2009)]]
Rubio debuted in the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] in the 2005–06 season with [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]]. Rubio was the youngest player ever to debut in the ACB, at 14 years and 11 months.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/04/doncic-youngest-player-to-make-debut-for-real-madrid|title=Doncic, youngest player to make debut for Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid|access-date=July 2, 2018|date=April 30, 2015}}</ref> He won the [[FIBA EuroChallenge]] championship with Joventut that year. He led the Spanish ACB League in steals during the 2006–07 season. He also won the Spanish ACB League's [[ACB Rising Star Award|Rising Star Award]] that season. Rubio was also named the [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Young Player of the Year]] in 2007, 2008, and 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2021/qualifiers|title=FIBA EuroBasket Qualifiers 2021|website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref> He made his [[EuroLeague]] debut on 24 October 2006, versus [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]] of [[Athens]] as Joventut's backup point guard for [[Elmer Bennett]]. He became the fifth-youngest EuroLeague player at the time. Rubio averaged 2.8 assists per game in his first season of EuroLeague play. He won the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] championship with Joventut in 2008. He was also voted [[All-Liga ACB Team|the Spanish ACB League's best point guard]] in 2008 and 2010. He won the [[2009–10 Euroleague|2009–10 EuroLeague]] with FC Barcelona.

Despite his notability, he was carefully shielded. [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]] and Rubio's parents agreed not to make him available for interviews until his 18th birthday on 21 October 2008.<ref name="Sweet16">{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8109/180/item |title=Sweet 16: Joventut's Rubio steals the show |work=Euroleague.net |date=February 13, 2007}}</ref> The restrictions were ended a few months early once he was selected for the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]] that would play at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Olympics]].<ref name="La Pistola">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?id=3469578 |title=La Pistola |first=Chad |last=Nielsen |work=[[ESPN The Magazine]] |date=July 1, 2008 |access-date=December 17, 2008}}</ref>

Rubio won the 2008 [[Mr. Europa|Mr. Europa Award]], which was given out yearly by the Italian [[Superbasket Magazine]]. In 2009, his club Badalona raised the amount of money his contract paid per year from 80,000 euros [[net income]] to 300,000 euros net income.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketme.com/2.0/noticia.php?id=23104|title=BasketMe.COM|website=www.basketme.com|access-date=24 January 2009|archive-date=23 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220923184610/https://www.basketme.com/2.0/noticia.php?id=23104|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named the Defensive Player of the Year for the Spanish ACB League 2008–09 season, and he also led the league in steals that season. Rubio declared himself eligible for the [[2009 NBA draft]] on 20 April 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2009/04/20/baloncesto/acb/1240233918.html|title=Ricky Rubio confirma que se inscribirá en el 'draft' - MARCA.com|website=www.marca.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4084579|title=NBA Draft: Ricky Rubio to enter NBA draft - ESPN|date=April 20, 2009}}</ref> Rubio's agent during that time was [[Dan Fegan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.interbasket.net/news/2036/2009/04/ricky-rubio-declares-for-2009-nba-draft/|title=Ricky Rubio declares for 2009 NBA Draft|first=Ed|last=Ziti|date=April 21, 2009}}</ref>

===Barcelona (2009–2011)===
After the 2009 NBA draft, Rubio played for the [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] for the next two seasons as agreed upon with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. During that time, he helped the team win the [[EuroLeague]] Championship in 2010 and the [[Liga ACB]] Championship in 2011.

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2011–2017)===
On 24 June 2009, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] acquired the fifth pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]], [[Etan Thomas]], [[Darius Songaila]] and [[Oleksiy Pecherov]] from the [[Washington Wizards]], in exchange for [[Randy Foye]] and [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]].<ref>{{cite web|date=June 24, 2009|title=Wolves Acquire the No. 5 Pick in 2009 NBA Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Acquire_the_No_5_Pick_-090624.html|access-date=June 24, 2009|work=NBA.com/Timberwolves|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc}}</ref> With the 5th pick, Minnesota selected Rubio, making him the first player born in the 1990s to be drafted with [[Steph Curry]] still on the board.<ref>Taylor, Nate. [http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/49150517.html Last first-round pick delivers guard only sweep] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090705144744/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/49150517.html|date=5 July 2009}}, ''[[Minneapolis Star-Tribune]]'', 26 June 2009.</ref> The Timberwolves had a total of four first-round picks in the 2009 NBA draft. They used the 6th and 18th picks in the first round and chose two other point guards, [[Jonny Flynn]] from [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] and [[Ty Lawson]] from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], surprising many in the NBA.<ref name="Knicks' interest">{{cite web|last=Sheridan|first=Chris|date=June 26, 2009|title=Knicks' interest heightens Rubio hype|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4290401|access-date=June 27, 2009}}</ref><ref name="Skeets">{{cite news|last=Skeets|first=J. E.|date=June 26, 2009|title=Report: Ricky Rubio's father says son may remain in Spain|work=Yahoo! Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/blog/ball_dont_lie/post/Report-Ricky-Rubio-s-father-says-son-may-remain?urn=nba,172985|access-date=June 26, 2009}}</ref> Lawson's draft rights were soon traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name="Skeets" /> The Timberwolves then used the 28th pick to select [[Wayne Ellington]], a shooting guard from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].

The following day, Rubio's father told a Spanish media outlet his son might return to Spain for at least one more season.<ref name="Knicks' interest" /> Rubio did not attend an introductory press conference by the Timberwolves.<ref name="Rubio won't">{{cite news|date=June 26, 2009|title=Rubio won't be at Wolves press conference|work=USA Today|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2009-06-26-4085123955_x.htm|access-date=June 26, 2009}}</ref> Rubio had a buyout clause in his Joventut contract reported by various media outlets as ranging from $6.6 million to $8.2 million, and Timberwolves general manager [[David Kahn (sports executive)|David Kahn]] admitted Rubio would probably have to play one more season in Spain to reduce or avoid the buyout.<ref name="Rubio won't" />

On 22 July, the [[Associated Press]] reported Rubio was seeking to leave Joventut, regardless of whether he was able to come to the NBA. The report indicated that the [[Liga ACB|ACB]] powers [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] were both interested in signing Rubio if he could not immediately go to the NBA. The main stumbling block to Rubio's NBA move was a clause in the league's collective bargaining agreement that prohibited a team from paying more than $500,000 toward a player's contract buyout. Barça and Real, as ACB clubs, were not subject to this rule and could pay far more toward a buyout.<ref>{{cite news|date=July 22, 2009|title=Rubio plans to leave DKV Joventut|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4348398|access-date=July 23, 2009}}</ref> In another development, the ''[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]'' reported on 4 August Rubio's representatives had been actively seeking endorsement deals in Minnesota to help finance his buyout (the NBA buyout rules are binding on teams, but not on third parties).<ref>{{cite news|last=Walters|first=Charley|date=August 4, 2009|title=Shooter Now: Team Rubio hasn't given up on Timberwolves; A's finally land prospect from Twins|newspaper=St. Paul Pioneer Press|url=http://www.twincities.com/timberwolves/ci_12989711?nclick_check=1|access-date=August 7, 2009}}</ref>

However, on 31 August 2009, [[ESPN]] reported Rubio would not come to the NBA until 2011 at the earliest.<ref name="Rubio to Barça" /> Joventut expressed a willingness to reduce the buyout, and the Timberwolves apparently had a deal to bring him to the NBA, but in the end Rubio did not feel ready to cross the Atlantic. Rubio issued the following statement:<ref name="Backing out" />

{{blockquote|The reason leading me to take this next step is to have a period of preparation to better take the challenge of the NBA in better conditions as a player. The Minnesota Timberwolves continue to be my first option and I wish to play with them in the near future.}}

Kahn believed Rubio and his family were being pressured by the Spanish media, his national teammates, and people in his hometown to stay in Spain, adding, "It's just been a tough summer. From an 18-year-old's perspective and his family's perspective, it was very nerve-racking".<ref name="Backing out" />

ESPN reported his original buyout with Joventut was [[Euro|€]]5.7 million ($8.1 million) in both 2009 and 2010.<ref name="Rubio to Barça" /> Barça bought out Rubio's contract for €3.5 million ($5.0 million), and announced on September 1 he had signed a six-year deal with the club. The contract gave him the option to go to the NBA after the 2010–11 season,<ref name="FCB release">{{cite press release|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/basquet/temporada09-10/09/n090901106510.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730184247/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/basquet/temporada09-10/09/n090901106510.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 30, 2012|title=Ricky Rubio signs for six seasons|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=September 1, 2009|access-date=September 1, 2009}}</ref> with ESPN reporting the buyout at that time would be a more manageable $1.4 million (of which the Timberwolves could pay $500,000).<ref name="Backing out" />

==== 2011–12 season ====
[[File:Ricky Rubio-MN v DET.jpg|thumb|left|Rubio in 2012]]
On 1 June 2011, sources reported Rubio had "reached an agreement with Minnesota to join the Timberwolves" for the [[2011–12 NBA season]].<ref name="wojnarowski1" /> Rubio arrived off a plane in Minnesota to a barrage of fans waiting to welcome him to the United States.<ref name="sbnation">{{cite web|url=http://minnesota.sbnation.com/minnesota-timberwolves/2011/6/20/2233841/ricky-rubio-minnesota-timberwolves-arrival-video|title=Ricky Rubio Has Arrived In Minnesota, Press Conference Set For Tuesday – SB Nation Minnesota|date=June 20, 2011|publisher=minnesota.sbnation.com|access-date=November 11, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Lee|last=Jenkins|title=¡olé!: For two years Ricky Rubio was an NBA draft pick stewing in his native Spain. Now he is spreading joy in Minnesota with his artful passes and spirited play|magazine=Sports Illustrated|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1193883/index.htm|access-date=January 23, 2012|archive-date=20 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120234011/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1193883/index.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 17 June 2011, Rubio held a press conference announcing he had signed with Minnesota.<ref name="sportingnews">{{cite web|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-06-21/timberwolves-rubio-wins-press-conference-games-will-be-harder|title=Timberwolves' Rubio wins press conference; games will be harder {{pipe}} NBA {{pipe}} Sporting News|publisher=aol.sportingnews.com|access-date=November 11, 2014}}</ref>

Becoming the 10th Spanish NBA player,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportyou.es/noticias/baloncesto/2011/12/27/el-bautismo-del-decimo-391427.html|title=Página no encontrada|website=SPORTYOU 20minutos}}</ref> Rubio made his regular season debut on 26 December 2011, to a sellout crowd at the [[Target Center]], the team's first sellout crowd since the 2007–08 season. Rubio recorded 6 points, 5 rebounds and 6 assists in 26 minutes in a 4-point loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.1500espn.com/sportswire/Ricky_Rubio_impresses_but_Wolves_fall_to_Thunder_in_sellout_opener122611|title=Ricky Rubio impresses but Wolves fall to Thunder in Sellout Opener|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111123454/http://www.1500espn.com/sportswire/Ricky_Rubio_impresses_but_Wolves_fall_to_Thunder_in_sellout_opener122611|archive-date=January 11, 2012}}</ref> He was named Western Conference [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]] after the first month of the season.<ref name="cbslocal">{{cite web|url=http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2012/02/01/rubio-named-west-conf-rookie-of-the-month/|title=Rubio Named West Conf. Rookie Of The Month « CBS Minnesota|date=February 2012|publisher=minnesota.cbslocal.com|access-date=November 11, 2014}}</ref> In February, Rubio and teammate [[Derrick Williams (basketball)|Derrick Williams]] were selected to participate in the 2012 Rising Stars challenge. Rubio was drafted to Team [[Shaquille O'Neal|Shaq]], while Williams was drafted to Team [[Charles Barkley|Chuck]]. Rubio scored 22 points on 19 February 2012 in a win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin Love's last-second FTs rally Wolves past Sixers|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320219016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220031549/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320219016|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 February 2012|work=ESPN|access-date=March 10, 2012|date=February 19, 2012}}</ref> In a loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on 9 March 2012, Rubio tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and his [[Fibular collateral ligament|lateral collateral ligament]] defending [[Kobe Bryant]]. He missed the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ricky Rubio has torn ACL|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7669679/minnesota-timberwolves-ricky-rubio-season-torn-acl|work=ESPN|access-date=March 10, 2012|date=March 9, 2012}}</ref><ref name="go">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7729283/minnesota-timberwolves-expect-ricky-rubio-back-6-9-months|title=Minnesota Timberwolves expect Ricky Rubio back in 6-9 months – ESPN|date=March 23, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=November 11, 2014}}</ref> Rubio finished second in Rookie of the Year voting, trailing only [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] rookie [[Kyrie Irving]].<ref name="foxsportsnorth">{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsportsnorth.com/05/15/12/Rubio-finishes-second-for-Rookie-of-the-/landing_timberwolves.html?blockID=729400&feedID=3697|title=North {{pipe}} FOX Sports|author=Fox Sports|publisher=foxsportsnorth.com|access-date=November 11, 2014}}</ref> Rubio had averaged 10.6 points, 8.2 assists and 2.2 steals in 41 games.

==== 2012–13 season ====
Rubio returned from his injury on 15 December 2012, in an overtime victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], playing for 19 minutes and totaling 9 assists and 8 points.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/12/16/sports/basketball/nba-roundup.html|title=Return of Ricky Rubio Gives Timberwolves a Boost Over Mavericks - The New York Times|newspaper=The New York Times|date=December 16, 2012}}</ref> He then recorded his first career triple-double with 21 points, 13 rebounds and 12 assists in a win over the San Antonio Spurs on 13 March 2013. Rubio almost recorded his second career triple-double in a loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on March 30 with 23 points, 10 rebounds and 9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130330/MEMMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Grizzlies 99, Timberwolves 86|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> Then on 13 April, he recorded a then career-high 24 points, 10 assists, 5 rebounds and 5 steals in a win over the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130413/PHXMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Timberwolves 105, Suns 93|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> Rubio finished the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]] with averages of 10.7 points, 7.3 assists and 2.4 steals per game. He also finished second in steals per game, behind [[Chris Paul]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2013_leaders.html|title=2012-13 NBA Leaders|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

==== 2013–14 season ====
On 11 November 2013, Rubio recorded his second career triple-double with 12 points, 14 assists and 10 rebounds in a 113–90 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131110/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Timberwolves 113, Lakers 90|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
In August 2006, Rubio led the rising junior Spain national team to the [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. During the tournament Rubio achieved two [[triple-double]]s and a [[quadruple-double]]. In the 110–106 double overtime finale victory over Russia, Rubio scored 51 points, the first player to do so in [[FIBA]] junior tournaments since [[Luol Deng]] (in 2001), grabbed 24 rebounds, made 12 assists, and stole the ball 7 times. He also forced the first overtime with a three-point, buzzer-beating shot from mid-court. Rubio was then named the [[Most Valuable Player]] of the tournament after leading it in points, rebounds, assists and steals.

===Senior national team===
The young Spaniard competed internationally with the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain National Team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Beijing Summer Olympics]]. The team included current and former NBA players such as [[Pau Gasol]], [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]], [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]], [[Marc Gasol]], [[Raül López (basketball)|Raúl López]], [[Jorge Garbajosa]], and [[Juan Carlos Navarro (basketball)|Juan Carlos Navarro]].

He played in the 2008 Olympics Basketball Tournament's gold medal game against the [[United States men's national basketball team|USA's]] [[2008 United States men's Olympic basketball team|"Redeem Team"]], and at 17 became the youngest player in an Olympic basketball final. The team took the silver medal after a loss at the gold, 118–107. The team continued international play at the [[2009 EuroBasket]] in Poland, where Spain defeated [[Serbian national basketball team|Serbia]] for the gold medal, 85–63. Rubio's contribution averaged 22.7 minutes, 5.9 points, 2.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 1.4 steals per game.

Rubio led Spain to a gold medal in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in China. They beat Argentina in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup Final|final]], 95–75.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/spain-recapture-fiba-basketball-world-cup-title-in-china|title=Spain recapture FIBA Basketball World Cup title in China|work=FIBA.basketball|access-date=September 17, 2019}}</ref> Rubio was chosen as one of the FIBA World Cup All-Star Five alongside Serbian's [[Bogdan Bogdanović (basketball)|Bogdan Bogdanovic]], France's [[Evan Fournier]], Spain's [[Marc Gasol]], and Argentina's [[Luis Scola]]. He was also named the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup Most Valuable Player|World Cup MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fibawc/935212/mvp-ricky-rubio-headlines-fiba-world-cup-all-star-five/|title=MVP Ricky Rubio headlines FIBA World Cup All-Star five|date=September 15, 2019|work=Eurohoops|access-date=September 17, 2019}}</ref> Rubio was named the [[Spanish Sportsman of the Year]], in 2019.

In the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament#Quarterfinals|Tokyo 2020 Olympics]] he broke the record for most points scored against Team USA with 38 points. The previous record was 35 points by [[Butch Lee]] in the [[Basketball at the 1976 Summer Olympics|1976 Montreal Olympics]].{{citation needed|date=March 2023}}
